study_identification_part.si4_title: Dissimilarity in Sulcal Width Patterns in the Cortex can be Used to Identify Patients With Schizophrenia With Extreme Deficits in Cognitive Performance

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: To investigate whether lifespan person-based similarity index for sulcal width (PBSI-SW) trajectories differ between patients with schizophrenia and healthy subjects, whether such differences are driven by individuals with extremely deviating PBSI-SW, and whether extreme PBSI-SW deviance is associated with deficits in cognition and sulcation index.

nm4_response_variable.answer: Person-based similarity index for sulcal width (PBSI-SW); based on sulcal width for 11 bilateral sulcal regions
nm4_response_variable.reason: The response variable is PBSI-SW, which is calculated from sulcal width measurements across 11 bilateral cortical regions. PBSI-SW is a multivariate summary measure that quantifies the similarity of an individual's sulcal width profile to the profiles of healthy controls.
nm4_response_variable.supporting_text: At each time point and for each individual, we computed a PBSI-SW value using a 3-step procedure ... First, we created the SW profile of each participant by concatenating her/his SW for 11 bilateral sulcal regions. Second, for each of the Nc controls, we calculated the Spearman's rank correlation coefficients between the participant's SW profile and the profiles of the other Nc - 1 controls. For each patient, we calculated the interindividual Spearman's rank correlation coefficient between the participant's SW profile and the profiles of all Nc controls. Third, for each control, a PBSI-SW was calculated as the average of the Nc - 1 correlation coefficients. For each patient, a PBSI-SW was calculated as the average of the Nc correlation coefficients.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: To assess the impact of deviance on PBSI-SW lifespan trajectories, GAMM models were recalculated without outliers (patients and controls with |PBSI-SW-Z| > 2). To investigate whether outlier patients shared differential characteristics, Welch t-tests were used to compare outlier vs non-outlier patients on: age at baseline, sex, PANSS total and subscale scores at baseline, illness duration, estimated IQ at baseline, and sulcation index at baseline and follow-up. Nonparametric permutation testing (1000 permutations) was used to validate the IQ comparison given unbalanced sample sizes. Chi-square tests were used to assess whether the proportion of patients with PBSI-SW-Z < -2 differed from controls, and whether outlier patients disproportionally showed decrease in PBSI-SW-Z between baseline and follow-up. Image quality metrics were compared between outlier and non-outlier patients. Regional contributions to PBSI-SW were compared between groups using Welch t-tests with FDR correction for multiple comparisons. Correlations between PBSI-SW and medication use/PANSS changes were also assessed. Effect sizes reported as Cohen's d.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: A small subgroup of patients (19 out of 164, 11.6%) showed markedly deviant PBSI-SW (Z < -2), which was associated with significantly lower estimated IQ (mean difference -9.66 points) and lower sulcation index at follow-up compared to non-outlier patients; the progressive reduction of PBSI-SW in schizophrenia relative to controls was driven by these deviating individuals.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: The PBSI-SW trajectories differed significantly between patients and controls (age-by-diagnosis interaction: F=14.57, P<.001), with patients showing a close to linear reduction with age while controls showed an increase until age 30 then stability. Cross-sectionally, patients had lower PBSI-SW than controls at follow-up (mean difference=0.02, Cohen's d=0.36, P=.001). Nineteen patients (11.6%) had PBSI-SW-Z < -2 at any timepoint compared to 10 controls (6.1%, χ²=3.06, P=.04). Of these 19 outlier patients, 16 showed decreased PBSI-SW-Z between baseline and follow-up (χ²=8.89, P<.01). When outliers were excluded, the age × diagnosis interaction was no longer significant (F=1.217, P=.139). Outlier patients had significantly lower estimated IQ at baseline compared to non-outlier patients (mean 89.00 vs 98.66, t=-3.32, P<.01, Cohen's d=-0.62) and lower sulcation index at follow-up (mean 1.60 vs 1.65, t=-2.40, P=.03, Cohen's d=-0.76). Outlier and non-outlier patients did not differ in age, sex, scanner, PANSS scores, illness duration, or image quality metrics. In controls, outliers did not differ from non-outliers in IQ or sulcation index. PBSI calculated from cortical thickness (PBSI-CT) did not show progressive changes or IQ differences between outliers and non-outliers. Regional contributions to PBSI-SW showed a similar pattern across controls, non-outlier patients, and outlier patients.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: Small sample size of outlier patients (n=19, with only 13 having IQ data) limits clinical characterization; lack of information about development and premorbid adjustment; estimated IQ from 4 WAIS subtests may have limitations compared to full-scale IQ; cannot rule out subtle effects of illness severity on image quality (e.g., more severely ill patients moving during scan); single-site study limiting generalizability
caa10_key_limitations.supporting_text: Although we did not find differences between outliers and nonoutliers on imaging quality metrics, we cannot rule out subtle effects (eg, more severely ill patients moving slightly more during scan acquisition and taking more medication) on the results ... IQ was estimated from the performances on 4 subtests of the Wechsler Adult Intelligence Scale III; this procedure may show some limitations in particular populations relative to using full-scale IQ scores ... Although we assessed a large sample of patients with schizophrenia, the small proportion of patients with considerable deviance in PBSI-SW led to small sample sizes for the clinical and cognitive characterization ... we did not have information about development or premorbid adjustment.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: The study introduced an extension of the person-based similarity index (PBSI) to index morphometric dissimilarity of individual patients relative to healthy controls. PBSI-SW is calculated using Spearman rank correlations of sulcal width profiles across 11 bilateral cortical regions. The approach explicitly leverages interindividual heterogeneity to identify biologically homogeneous subgroups. The study also compared PBSI-SW with PBSI-CT (cortical thickness), finding that sulcal width was more sensitive to schizophrenia-associated progressive changes. A leave-one-region-out method was used to assess regional contributions to PBSI-SW. The correlation between the study's Z-score calculation and the Nispat method was 0.94, validating the approach.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: This study focuses on sulcal width rather than traditional cortical thickness or volume measures, motivated by sulcal width's sensitivity to changes in adjacent gyri, subcortical white matter, and sulcal cytoarchitecture. The PBSI approach combines concepts of morphometric similarity and interindividual heterogeneity. The sulcation index, which measures the ratio between total sulcal surface area and brain hull area, was used as a marker of perinatal neurodevelopmental perturbations. Eleven bilateral sulcal regions were defined based on prior studies (Penttilä et al. 2009, Sarrazin et al. 2018). The study used two scanners (Philips Intera or Achieva 1.5T) with the same vendor, field strength, and acquisition protocol, and all participants had baseline and follow-up scans on the same scanner. The R script used for PBSI-SW calculation is available from GitHub. The study also examined symmetrized annual percent change (APC) for PBSI-SW and assessed its relationship with image quality. Antipsychotic medication data were available for only 50% of patients (82 out of 164).
